questions.q: About how much water does a healthy adult gain per day in total from drinks, food and metabolism?
questions.explain: Roughly 1,200 mL from drinks, 1,000 mL from food and 350 mL produced by metabolism, about 2,550 mL a day. In balance, the same amount is lost.

open.q: About how much water does a healthy adult gain per day in total from drinks, food and metabolism?

questions.q: How much metabolic water does the body produce per day?
questions.explain: Oxidation of food produces about 350 mL of water a day, on top of drinks (about 1,200 mL) and food (about 1,000 mL).

open.q: How much metabolic water does the body produce per day?

questions.q: Which route accounts for the largest daily water loss in a healthy adult?
options: Insensible loss from skin and lungs
questions.explain: Urine is about 1,500 mL a day, insensible loss about 900 mL, faeces about 100 mL and sweat about 50 mL in normal conditions.

open.q: Which route accounts for the largest daily water loss in a healthy adult?

questions.q: What is meant by insensible water loss, and about how much is lost per day?
options: Sweating in hot weather, about 900 mL
Evaporation from skin and lungs, about 900 mL
Water lost in faeces, about 100 mL
Urine passed each day, about 1,500 mL
questions.explain: It is called insensible because it is not noticed. It continues even in cold weather and is separate from visible sweating.

open.q: What is meant by insensible water loss, and about how much is lost per day?

questions.q: What is the main route by which sodium leaves the body in health?
questions.explain: Nearly all sodium loss is through the kidneys. Sweat and faeces each lose only a small amount, so the kidney controls sodium balance.

open.q: What is the main route by which sodium leaves the body in health?

questions.q: Severe diarrhoea mainly causes loss of which of these?
questions.explain: Diarrhoea loses water and sodium, along with bicarbonate and potassium, which can lead to dehydration and metabolic acidosis.

open.q: Severe diarrhoea mainly causes loss of which substances from the body?

questions.q: Which condition causes loss of water alone, as very dilute urine?
questions.explain: Diabetes insipidus is a lack of ADH or of the kidney's response to it. Diabetes mellitus loses water and glucose, haemorrhage loses water and all electrolytes, and sweating loses water and sodium.

open.q: Which condition causes loss of water alone, as very dilute urine?

questions.q: Which of these is a cause of fluid overload (excess fluid gain)?
questions.explain: Fluid excess follows over-transfusion, over-hydration or excessive water drinking (polydipsia). The other options all lose fluid.

open.q: Name a cause of fluid overload (excess fluid gain).

questions.q: What mainly determines the volume of the extracellular fluid?
options: The total amount of sodium in the body
questions.explain: Sodium and its associated anions make up about 90% of ECF solute, so changes in total body sodium cause matching changes in ECF volume, which in turn drives the controls on sodium excretion.

open.q: What mainly determines the volume of the extracellular fluid?

options: Increased sodium retention when arterial pressure rises
Increased sodium excretion when arterial pressure rises
Sodium loss caused by diuretic drugs
Increased potassium loss when pressure falls
questions.explain: A rise in arterial pressure acts directly on the tubules to reduce sodium reabsorption and also suppresses the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system, so more sodium and water are excreted and pressure returns toward normal.

accept: more sodium excreted when blood pressure rises
increased sodium excretion with raised blood pressure

questions.q: What happens to sodium excretion when arterial blood pressure falls?
options: It falls, because the renin-angiotensin system is stimulated and tubules retain sodium
It is unchanged, because blood pressure has no effect on how the kidney handles sodium
It rises, because aldosterone secretion is switched off when pressure drops
It rises, because the tubules reabsorb less sodium to lower the blood volume
questions.explain: A fall in pressure stimulates renin release and enhances sodium reabsorption directly in the tubules, so sodium and water are retained.

open.q: What happens to sodium excretion when arterial blood pressure falls, and why?
